BL-2363 INVESTIGATION: CACHE COMPONENT FEATURES
================================================

Author: Kevin, CIS3590 Team 7
Date:   Oct 12, 2026
Repos:  ortus-boxlang/BoxLang (core) and ortus-boxlang/boxlang-web-support,
        both on the development branch as of Oct 12, 2026.


SUMMARY
-------

BL-2363 is not development-ready: its two central attributes, useQueryString
and expireURL, depend on page-level caching that BoxLang does not have yet,
and that work spans both the core BoxLang repo and boxlang-web-support. Per
guidance from the BoxLang maintainers (Oct 2026), this document records
Team 7's investigation instead of an implementation.

Key findings:

- The cache component (bx:cache / cfcache) in core only caches content
  between the tags and objects (put/get). Full-page caching is an open TODO
  in the code.
- useQueryString and expireURL only make sense once cached content is tied
  to a request URL. Core has no URL; the web runtime does, through the cgi
  scope.
- The web runtime's handler for clientcache/servercache listens on
  onComponentInvocation, but core announces onCacheComponentAction. Core
  never announces onComponentInvocation anywhere, so that handler appears
  never to run (see section 3).
- region and the legacy username/password/port/protocol attributes do not
  depend on the web runtime and could be closed independently.

A working prototype of all seven attributes in core exists on the team
branch (section 9). It is a reference, not a proposed PR.


1. WHAT BL-2363 ASKS FOR
------------------------

The ticket asks to implement seven cfcache attributes that the BoxLang cache
component declares but never uses. Its description is only this snippet:

    new Attribute( Key.expireURL, "string", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "wildcarded URL reference"
    new Attribute( Key.password, "string", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "password"
    new Attribute( Key.port, "integer", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "port number"
    new Attribute( Key.protocol, "string", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "http://|https://"
    new Attribute( Key.region, "string", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "region_name"
    new Attribute( Key.useQueryString, "boolean", false, Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "false|true"
    new Attribute( Key.username, "string", Set.of( Validator.NOT_IMPLEMENTED ) ), // "username"

The snippet is out of date. Commit "BL-2324 remove validation for now"
(Apr 24, 2026) removed the NOT_IMPLEMENTED validators. Since then, these
attributes are ACCEPTED AND SILENTLY IGNORED rather than rejected with an
error. A CFML app migrated to BoxLang that relies on them runs without
complaint but behaves differently.

What each attribute means in Adobe ColdFusion (cfcache reference):

  useQueryString      Include the query string in the page cache ID, so each
                      query-string variation is cached separately. Default
                      false. Added in ColdFusion 9; before that the query
                      string was always part of the ID.
  expireURL           With action="flush", flush only cached pages whose URL
                      matches a wildcard pattern, e.g. **/view.cfm?id=**.
                      Matching rules are not specified.
  region              Name of the cache region to use. Added in ColdFusion 10.
  username, password  Credentials for a page that needs web-server
                      authentication, used by the server's internal request
                      to the page.
  port, protocol      Port and http:// / https:// used to build the cached
                      page's URL; default to the current page's values.

The ticket gives no written acceptance criteria.


2. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS IN CORE
------------------------------

The component lives in
src/main/java/ortus/boxlang/runtime/components/cache/Cache.java
(428 lines on development, Oct 12, 2026). It handles object caching and
caching of the content between its tags; it hands two web-only actions to
interceptors.

  Action                    What core does today
  ------------------------  -------------------------------------------------
  get                       Reads key from the chosen cache into the name
                            variable. key required.
  put                       Stores value (or the rendered body) under key.
                            key required.
  cache, optimal, content   All three behave the same: getOrSet on the
                            rendered body. Only the content between the tags
                            is cached, never the whole page.
  flush                     Clears one key, or the whole cache when no key is
                            given.
  delete                    Clears one key. Present in the CacheAction enum,
                            but "delete" is missing from the action validator,
                            so action="delete" is likely rejected before it
                            runs.
  clientcache, servercache  Not handled in core. Core announces
                            onCacheComponentAction and throws if no
                            interceptor sets a result.

Other working behavior:

- Cache selection: cacheName picks a named cache via
  context.getApplicationCache(); directory creates a file-backed cache
  (FileSystemStore) on first use; otherwise the default cache.
- Timeouts: timespan and idleTime are in days (or a Duration), converted to
  seconds. If only idleTime is given, it is also used as timespan.
- Generated keys: when no key (or alias id) is passed, the key is
  BL_TEMPLATE_ + hash40() of the attributes struct and the ComponentBody.
  Nothing about the request URL is in the key.
- Other attributes in use: useCache=false bypasses the cache;
  stripWhitespace trims string results; throwOnError switches between
  get/getQuiet and clear/clearQuiet.
- Tests: src/test/java/ortus/boxlang/runtime/components/cache/CacheTest.java
  covers cfcache/bx:cache in script and template syntax, object and content
  caching, named caches, directory caches and flush. It has no test for any
  BL-2363 attribute or for delete.


3. WHAT IS MISSING
------------------

The biggest gap is page caching itself; the BL-2363 attributes sit on top
of it.

- Full-page server caching
    Where: Cache.java, case CACHE/OPTIMAL/CONTENT
    Marked "// TODO: Need to figure out how to handle the full page
    caching". A body-less <cfcache> at the top of a page does not cache the
    page.
- clientcache / servercache in the web runtime
    Where: boxlang-web-support interceptors/WebRequest.java
    Handler appears never to run (below).
- useQueryString, expireURL
    Where: Cache.java constructor
    Declared under "// TODO: These are specfic to web connectivity...",
    never read.
- region
    Where: Cache.java. Declared, never read.
- username, password, port, protocol
    Where: Cache.java. Declared, never read. Javadoc already calls protocol
    and port "Legacy CFML attribute. Not implemented".
- dependsOn (not in BL-2363)
    Where: Cache.java. Declared with "// TODO: Circle back and immplement
    find nearby checks for these variables - then make them part of the key".
- action="delete"
    Where: Cache.java. Enum value and case exist; "delete" missing from the
    validator list.

Smaller issues noticed: Key.metadata is declared twice in the attribute list,
and the put failure path logs "An error occurred while attempting to flush
the cache".

The client/server cache handler appears never to fire
.....................................................

Core announces one event; the web runtime listens on a different one:

- Core, Cache.java line 262:
  interceptorService.announce( BoxEvent.ON_CACHE_COMPONENT_ACTION, interceptorArgs )
  i.e. the event "onCacheComponentAction".
- Web runtime, WebRequest.java: the cache logic is in a method annotated
  @InterceptionPoint named onComponentInvocation.
- InterceptorPool.register() subscribes each @InterceptionPoint method to the
  event with the same name as the method.
- BoxEvent.ON_COMPONENT_INVOCATION ("onComponentInvocation") is defined, but
  a search of all 1,606 Java files in core src/main/java found no place that
  announces it.

So in a web request, action="clientcache" or "servercache" most likely throws
"is not valid in the current runtime" instead of setting a Cache-Control
header. By contrast, the file component's handler is named
onFileComponentAction, which matches BoxEvent.ON_FILECOMPONENT_ACTION. We
traced this by reading code and did not run it; boxlang-web-support has no
test covering these two actions. This likely explains part of the
maintainers' note that client- and server-side caching is not implemented
yet.


4. HOW useQueryString SHOULD WORK AND WHAT IT DEPENDS ON
--------------------------------------------------------

useQueryString changes how a page cache ID is built, so it cannot work until
cached content is identified by the page it came from.

Expected behavior, from the ACF reference:

- useQueryString="false" (default): view.cfm?id=1 and view.cfm?id=2 share one
  cached copy.
- useQueryString="true": the query string becomes part of the cache ID, so
  each variation gets its own copy.
- Before ColdFusion 9 the query string was always part of the ID;
  ColdFusion 9 added useQueryString with a default of false, which changed
  that (Ben Forta, 2011). BoxLang should follow the modern behavior.
- When true, dependsOn also considers URL parameters. dependsOn is itself
  unimplemented.

What it depends on:

1. A cache ID tied to the page. Today's generated key (BL_TEMPLATE_ + hash
   of attributes and body) has no page or URL in it. Some notion of "which
   page" must be added first.
2. The request URL. Only available in a web request, from the web runtime
   (section 5). Outside a web request there is no URL, so behavior there
   needs a decision.
3. Page caching, for the full ACF meaning. In ACF, useQueryString mostly
   matters for whole-page caching, which BoxLang lacks. Whether it should
   also apply to content caching between tags is unconfirmed.
4. expireURL depends on the same thing. Flushing by URL pattern only works if
   each cache entry records its URL, in its key or its metadata. The two
   attributes should be designed together.


5. WHERE THE PAGE URL COMES FROM, AND HOW THE REPOS CONNECT
-----------------------------------------------------------

Core has no page URL of its own; in a web request, boxlang-web-support
exposes it through the cgi scope, which core code can read but not depend on.

  BoxLang core (no request URL)          boxlang-web-support (has the URL)
  +-------------------------------+      +-----------------------------------+
  | Cache component (Cache.java)  |      | WebRequestBoxContext              |
  | builds keys, picks a cache,   |      | one per HTTP request; owns the    |
  | runs actions                  |      | exchange; registers url, form,    |
  +-------------------------------+      | cgi and cookie scopes             |
      |     ^     |                      +-----------------------------------+
      |     |     |                                       |
      |     |     |                      +-----------------------------------+
      |     +-----|---- read via --------| CGIScope                          |
      |           |     getScope("cgi")  | script_name, query_string,        |
      v           |                      | request_url                       |
  +---------------+---------------+      +-----------------------------------+
  | Cache providers and filters   |
  | ICacheProvider, WildcardFilter|      +-----------------------------------+
  +-------------------------------+      | WebRequest interceptor            |
                  |                      | listens on onComponentInvocation; |
                  +-- announces ----X--> | sets Cache-Control for            |
                      onCacheComponent   | clientcache / servercache         |
                      Action             +-----------------------------------+

  X = names differ: core announces onCacheComponentAction, but the handler
      listens on onComponentInvocation, which core never announces, so
      client/server caching never reaches it.

How the repos connect. boxlang-web-support compiles against the core jar
(its build.gradle uses ../boxlang/build/libs/boxlang-<version>.jar when
present). It imports core classes such as Cache and Cache.CacheAction
directly. Core never imports web-support. The two talk at runtime in two
ways:

- Interceptor events: core announces an event (onCacheComponentAction,
  onFileComponentAction) with a data struct; web-support's WebRequest
  interceptor handles it and writes a result back.
- Contexts and scopes: each web request runs in a WebRequestBoxContext,
  created in WebRequestExecutor. It owns the HTTP exchange (IBoxHTTPExchange)
  and registers the url, form, cgi and cookie scopes. Core code can ask any
  context for a scope by name, context.getScope( Key.of( "cgi" ) ); outside a
  web request this throws ScopeNotFoundException. A component can also test
  context.getParentOfType( WebRequestBoxContext.class ), which is what
  WebRequest.java does, but that needs a web-support class.

Where the URL pieces come from (boxlang-web-support .../scopes/CGIScope.java,
each computed lazily from the exchange):

  CGI key            Source in the exchange     Example
  -----------------  -------------------------  ---------------------------
  cgi.script_name    getRequestURI()            /products/view.cfm
  cgi.query_string   getRequestQueryString()    id=1
  cgi.path_info      getRequestPathInfo()       extra path after the script
  cgi.request_url    getRequestURL()            the full URL

There is no pageURL field or helper in either repo. In ACF terms, the "page
URL" is the script path plus, when useQueryString is true, the query string;
in BoxLang that means cgi.script_name and cgi.query_string. When none of
these exist, there is no page to cache by URL.


6. LIKELY SPLIT BETWEEN CORE AND WEB-SUPPORT
--------------------------------------------

Core should own the cache logic and key format; web-support should own
anything that needs the HTTP request or response. This matches how
clientcache/servercache and file uploads are already split.

- region as alias for cacheName
    Core. Cache selection only; no web dependency.
- username, password, port, protocol as accepted-but-ignored
    Core. BoxLang does not cache pages by making an HTTP request to itself,
    so there is nothing to connect to.
- Page cache key format (where the URL goes in the key or metadata)
    Core. Shared by useQueryString and expireURL; the cache providers live
    in core.
- expireURL flush by pattern
    Core. Only matches stored keys; needs no request.
- Supplying the current page URL and query string
    Web-support, or core reading the cgi scope. The open design choice
    (section 8).
- Full-page caching (cache and replay a whole response, stop the page early)
    Both. Core decides hit or miss; web-support owns the response buffer and
    headers.
- clientcache / servercache headers
    Web-support. Already there; the event name needs fixing in one of the
    two repos.
- Web-request tests for useQueryString and full-page caching
    Web-support. Core tests run in ScriptingRequestBoxContext, which has no
    cgi scope. Web-support has MockHTTPExchange and BaseWebTest.


7. EXISTING CODE THAT CAN BE REUSED
-----------------------------------

- WildcardFilter
    core runtime/cache/filters/WildcardFilter.java
    For expireURL. Turns * and ? into a regex, case-insensitive by default,
    full-key match. ** collapses to *, so ACF-style **/view.cfm?id=**
    patterns work.
- ICacheProvider.clearAll( ICacheKeyFilter )
    core runtime/cache/providers/ICacheProvider.java
    Clearing every key that matches a filter. RegexFilter is in the same
    package.
- CACHE_PREFIX (BL_TEMPLATE_)
    Cache.java
    Marks generated page/content keys, so a flush can target only those and
    never user keys.
- Alias pattern (id -> key, idleTime -> timespan)
    Cache.java _invoke()
    The model for region -> cacheName.
- "Accepted for compatibility" pattern
    File.java ("// ACF compatibility attribute"), Dump.java
    The model for username/password/port/protocol: declare with a comment,
    no logic.
- ON_CACHE_COMPONENT_ACTION + WebRequest interceptor
    core Cache.java; web-support interceptors/WebRequest.java
    Hand-off pattern for anything that needs the request.
- CGIScope
    web-support scopes/CGIScope.java
    Source of script_name, query_string, request_url.
- MockHTTPExchange, BaseWebTest
    web-support src/test/java/.../web/util/
    Web-request tests in web-support.


8. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE MAINTAINERS
-------------------------------------

1.  Full-page caching first? Should BL-2363 wait for full-page server
    caching, or should useQueryString/expireURL also apply to content cached
    between tags?
2.  How core gets the URL. Read the cgi scope from core when present, or add
    an event (or extend onCacheComponentAction) so web-support supplies the
    path?
3.  Event name mismatch. Is WebRequest.onComponentInvocation meant to receive
    onCacheComponentAction? If so, which side should change: rename the
    web-support method, or have core announce onComponentInvocation?
4.  Client-side caching requirements. What should clientcache, and the
    client half of cache/optimal, do beyond setting Cache-Control? The
    maintainers flagged this as unresolved.
5.  Where the URL is stored. In the key (BL_TEMPLATE_<path>|<hash>) or in
    entry metadata? Keys are simpler to filter; metadata keeps keys
    unchanged but needs a metadata filter.
6.  Key stability. Generated keys hash the ComponentBody object. Is that hash
    stable across requests and recompiles, or can identical content get
    different keys?
7.  Behavior outside a web request. Ignore useQueryString and expireURL
    silently, log, or throw?
8.  Upgrade impact. Adding the path to generated keys means entries cached
    before an upgrade are missed once. Acceptable?
9.  Legacy attributes. Is "accept and ignore" correct for username,
    password, port, protocol, or should they log or warn?
10. region precedence. If both cacheName and region are passed, should
    cacheName win, or should it be an error?
11. Small fixes outside the ticket. Should "delete" be added to the action
    validator, and the duplicate metadata attribute removed, as separate
    tickets?


9. RECOMMENDATION AND POSSIBLE APPROACH
---------------------------------------

Split BL-2363: close the parts with no web dependency now, and fold
useQueryString and expireURL into the page-caching work.

1. Small core ticket (ready now): region as an alias for cacheName, and
   username/password/port/protocol declared as accepted-but-ignored CFML
   compatibility attributes, with docs and tests. Optionally add "delete" to
   the action validator.
2. Fix the event wiring: make clientcache/servercache reach WebRequest
   (rename the handler to onCacheComponentAction, or announce
   onComponentInvocation from core), and add web-support tests using
   MockHTTPExchange.
3. Design page caching: decide how a cached page is identified, where its URL
   is stored, and how a full response is captured and replayed. This is the
   dependency the maintainers identified.
4. Then useQueryString and expireURL: core builds page keys as
   BL_TEMPLATE_<path>[?query]|<hash> (or stores the path in metadata), and
   flush with expireURL calls
   clearAll( new WildcardFilter( "BL_TEMPLATE_" + expireURL + "*" ) ).
   Web-support supplies the path, via the cgi scope or an event.
5. Test across both repos: web-support's build already picks up a locally
   built core jar, so both changes can be tested together before either PR.

Prototype on the team branch
............................

Before the maintainers' guidance arrived, Team 7 implemented all seven
attributes in core as a proof of concept:
https://github.com/LivinKevin/BoxLang/tree/BL-2363-add-missing-cache-component-features

It will not be submitted as a PR, but shows one concrete version of steps 1
and 4:

- region alias and the legacy attributes, matching the patterns in
  section 7.
- A getRequestPath( context, includeQueryString ) helper that reads
  cgi.script_name and cgi.query_string, returning null when there is no cgi
  scope.
- Generated keys of the form BL_TEMPLATE_<path>|<hash>; unchanged outside a
  web request.
- expireURL flush with WildcardFilter.
- Five new CacheTest tests. useQueryString is only tested outside a web
  request, which is exactly the gap described in sections 6 and 8.

The cache tests passed on the team's last local run. Parts of it, especially
step 1, could be reused if the maintainers want that smaller ticket.
